title: Polymer clay butterfly hair comb
subtitle: A decorative butterfly mounted on a plain hair comb using polymer clay
excerpt: Two butterfly wings modelled from coloured polymer clay and attached to a plain metal or plastic hair comb after curing. The wings can be painted with detailed vein patterns or left as solid colours. No kiln is needed: the wings cure in a domestic oven at 130°C.

glossaryTerms.definition: A PVC-based modelling material that cures hard in a domestic oven at 110 to 130°C

content.text: A butterfly comb is a two-piece

project: each wing is modelled and cured separately, then both are glued to a plain hair comb with a strong adhesive. Curing the wings flat on a tile before assembly gives a controlled result. No kiln is required.

materials.name: Polymer clay, primary wing colour (orange, blue, or purple)
Polymer clay, dark brown or black (for wing borders)
Plain metal or plastic hair comb

content.text: Roll the main colour to 4 mm thick. Cut two wing shapes freehand with a fettling knife: each wing has a larger rounded upper lobe and a smaller pointed lower lobe. The upper lobe of each wing should be about 5 cm wide; the whole wing about 6 cm tall.

Roll thin strings of dark clay and press them onto each wing surface as border lines along the outer edge, following the wing silhouette. Add a few vein lines radiating from the wing root toward the outer edge.
Press the dark strings gently flat with a finger so they are level with the wing surface. Add small circular dots at the tips of the lower lobe.
Flatten the inside edge of each wing straight: this is where both wings will meet at the centre body of the butterfly.
Lay both wings flat on a ceramic tile and cure at 130°C for 25 minutes. Ventilate the kitchen. Allow to cool fully.

Position both wings on the comb with their inside edges meeting at the centre. The body of the butterfly sits where the wings join; you can add a thin roll of dark clay glued between the wings as a simple body. Glue each wing to the comb spine with cyanoacrylate adhesive, holding for 60 seconds. Allow to cure for 24 hours before wearing.

Add translucent polymer clay overlaid with mica powder to the main wing to give a metallic sheen under different lights. Make moth wings by using dusty grey and brown tones with circular eyespot markings.

items.problem: Dark border strings detach from the wing face during curing
items.cause: The strings were not pressed firmly enough into the wing surface before curing
items.fix: After curing, glue the detached strings back with cyanoacrylate. Press firmly and hold for a minute. Next time, use a roller to press the border strings fully flush before curing

items.problem: Wings warp upward at the edges during curing
items.cause: The clay was thinner at the edges and curled as it cured
items.fix: Cure with the wings weighted down by a small ceramic tile placed gently on top, leaving them flat as they cure. Alternatively, re-cure briefly at 100°C on a convex surface and press flat while warm
